pure-announcement.rationale: It is a promotional landing page for Qodo's survey report rather than a product launch, release note or funding announcement, and it does carry a transferable claim about validation lagging AI coding velocity.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (SIEM agentic visibility gap, OSV format, Code Mode for MCP, code knowledge graph) touch AI-generated-code incident rates or review burden.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The four headline statistics are attributed to a named survey of 500 U.S. IT engineers whose full report the reader can obtain and check.

durability.rationale: The note's substance is four percentages from a single 2026 vendor survey (89% incidents, 40% outages, 41% review time, 95% scrutiny) — point-in-time adoption figures that will be stale within a survey cycle.

actionability.rationale: It is a 'what you'll learn' teaser that withholds the report's actual findings, leaving a reader with a described landscape and no concrete practice to adopt beyond an implied nod toward automated gates.

atomicity.rationale: Everything on the page serves one paragraph-sized claim: organizations have accelerated AI code generation faster than the validation systems needed to catch its failures.
